## Rate limits

All API calls: 180 requests per minute on a rolling window, 429 when exceeded.

More on limitsLess

Bulk APIs: additional 3 requests/second and max 10 records per request. Webhook notifications: 600 per minute and 1,800 per 10 minutes per account.

## How to get an API key

Copper uses API key. The steps below follow Copper's own docs.

1.  Create a Copper account. API access starts on the Professional plan.
2.  Copper web app > System settings > API Keys > GENERATE API KEY; OAuth 2.0 for partner integrations
3.  Send it with every request: headers: X-PW-AccessToken: <API key>, X-PW-Application: developer\_api, X-PW-UserEmail: <email of key owner>, Content-Type: application/json.
4.  Make a first call: Atomically update the lead matching given criteria or create it. Match on name, email or a custom field (match.field\_name 'custom' with custom\_field\_definition\_id + value; the field must be available on Leads and filterable). 0 matches = create, 1 = update, >1 = 422 with matching IDs, >30 = 422 without IDs. Keep the key in an environment variable, never in the command.
    
    ```
    curl -X PUT "https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1/leads/upsert" \
      -H "X-PW-AccessToken: $COPPER_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{}'
    ```

## Strengths and limits

### Where it fits

-   Google Workspace teams that want a simple CRM inside Gmail
-   Upserting leads by a match field or custom field (PUT /leads/upsert)
-   People and companies with platform-enforced unique keys (person email, company email domain)

### Where it falls short

-   Bulk loads: 180 requests/minute overall, bulk endpoints max 10 records per request and 3 requests/second
-   Reliable event delivery: webhooks fire at most once and are never retried
-   Deep exports through search: search returns only the first 100,000 records
-   Copper Basic plan users: the pricing table shows 'API & Embedded integration SDK' (and Leads) only on Professional and Business

### Worth knowing

-   Webhooks are fire-once: no retries on any failure, so a down endpoint loses events; reconcile with periodic search. Source: [developer.copper.com/webhooks/overview.html](https://developer.copper.com/webhooks/overview.html)
-   Bulk endpoints accept only 10 records (422 'Request size too large, limit is 10') and have their own 3 req/s cap. Source: [developer.copper.com/companies/bulk-company-create.html](https://developer.copper.com/companies/bulk-company-create.html)
-   Three auth headers are required on every call, including X-PW-UserEmail of the key owner. Source: [developer.copper.com/introduction/requests.html](https://developer.copper.com/introduction/requests.html)
-   Company email domain and person email are unique keys; a bulk company create fails for any record whose email\_domains overlap an existing company. Source: [developer.copper.com/companies/bulk-company-create.html](https://developer.copper.com/companies/bulk-company-create.html)
-   Search stops at the first 100,000 records regardless of pagination. Source: [developer.copper.com/introduction/pagination.html](https://developer.copper.com/introduction/pagination.html)

4 moreShow fewer

-   API domain moved from api.prosperworks.com to api.copper.com. Source: [developer.copper.com](https://developer.copper.com/)
-   No API on the Basic plan: 'API & Embedded integration SDK' is ticked only for Professional and Business. Source: [copper.com/pricing](https://www.copper.com/pricing) (rendered comparison table)
-   Signup is Google-only, so every Copper account (and the X-PW-UserEmail header value) is a Google Workspace/Gmail identity.
-   The official MCP is announced for a November 2026 beta (Claude only, read-only); until then only third-party connectors exist, which Copper notes run on an admin API key. Source: [copper.com/mcp](https://www.copper.com/mcp)

## Who should use it

Use Copper for

Google Workspace teams that want a simple CRM inside Gmail

Look elsewhere for

Bulk loads: 180 requests/minute overall, bulk endpoints max 10 records per request and 3 requests/second

## Before you build

Four things to settle first, each read off Copper's own pages.

-   **Confirm the API is on your plan**API access starts on the Professional plan. Free tier: No free plan.
    
-   **Keep the key out of your code**API key. It is sent as: headers: X-PW-AccessToken: <API key>, X-PW-Application: developer\_api, X-PW-UserEmail: <email of key owner>, Content-Type: application/json.
    
-   **Design around the rate limit**All API calls: 180 requests per minute on a rolling window, 429 when exceeded.
    
-   **Know the catch before you scale**Webhooks are fire-once: no retries on any failure, so a down endpoint loses events; reconcile with periodic search. Source: [developer.copper.com/webhooks/overview.html](https://developer.copper.com/webhooks/overview.html)
